key_insight: A privacy-preserving Llama 3.3 70B pipeline achieved high accuracy in oncology registry abstraction, rather than cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support cancer research by converting clinical notes into structured registry data while keeping identifiable information within hospital infrastructure.
method: Extracted over 50 variables from 6,700 oncology notes without task-specific fine-tuning.
Used local Hide-In-Plain-Sight de-identification to protect patient information.
Classified outputs as correct, missing, spurious, or incorrect.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on 200 randomly sampled notes with adjudicated ground truth yielded F1 scores of 97.2% for diagnosis, 95.8% for histology, 92.6% for stage, 91.4% for biomarkers, and 88.1% for treatments.
watch_item: External testing covered only 50 notes and showed reduced performance for list-valued variables, leaving broader generalizability uncertain.
paper_title: Privacy-Preserving Large Language Model Deployment for Oncology Registry Abstraction: Structure-Aware Evaluation in a Real-World Clinical Setting
